sanskrit: so 'ham apy adya yāsyāmi gatiṃ pitṛniṣevitām na śaknomy ātmanātmānam ahaṃ dhārayituṃ śubhe
english: So I too shall this day go the way my father has gone; I cannot, fair one, hold up my own self by my own strength.

sanskrit: sā tvaṃ mayi mṛte mātas tathā gāṇḍīvadhanvani bhava prītimatī devi satyenātmānam ālabhe
english: When I am dead, mother, and likewise the bearer of the Gāṇḍīva, may you be content, O lady; by truth I take hold of my own self.

sanskrit: ity uktvā sa tadā rājā duḥkhaśokasamāhataḥ upaspṛśya mahārāja duḥkhād vacanam abravīt
english: Having spoken thus, the king, stricken with grief and sorrow, touched water, O great king, and out of anguish uttered these words.

sanskrit: śṛṇvantu sarvabhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca tvaṃ ca mātar yathā satyaṃ bravīmi bhujagottame
english: Let all beings hear, both the moving and the unmoving, and you too, mother, O excellent serpent-maiden, that I speak the truth.

sanskrit: yadi nottiṣṭhati jayaḥ pitā me bharatarṣabhaḥ asminn eva raṇoddeśe śoṣayiṣye kalevaram
english: If Jaya does not rise up, my father, that bull of the Bhāratas, here on this very field of battle I shall let my body waste away.

sanskrit: na hi me pitaraṃ hatvā niṣkṛtir vidyate kva cit narakaṃ pratipatsyāmi dhruvaṃ guruvadhārditaḥ
english: For having slain my father there is no atonement for me anywhere; tormented by the killing of my elder, I shall surely descend into hell.

sanskrit: vīraṃ hi kṣatriyaṃ hatvā gośatena pramucyate pitaraṃ tu nihatyaivaṃ dustarā niṣkṛtir mayā
english: One who slays a heroic Kṣatriya is freed by the gift of a hundred cows; but having slain my father in this way, hard to cross is the atonement for me.

sanskrit: eṣa hy eko mahātejāḥ pāṇḍuputro dhanaṃjayaḥ pitā ca mama dharmātmā tasya me niṣkṛtiḥ kutaḥ
english: For he was unique, the great-splendored son of Pāṇḍu, Dhanaṃjaya, and my father, righteous of soul; from where can there be atonement for me for his death?

sanskrit: ity evam uktvā nṛpate dhanaṃjayasuto nṛpaḥ upaspṛśyābhavat tūṣṇīṃ prāyopeto mahāmatiḥ
english: Having spoken thus, O king, the king who was Dhanaṃjaya's son touched water and fell silent, the great-minded one resolved to fast unto death.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca prāyopaviṣṭe nṛpatau maṇipūreśvare tadā pitṛśokasamāviṣṭe saha mātrā paraṃtapa
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the king, the lord of Maṇipūra, had thus sat down to fast unto death, overcome with grief for his father, together with his mother, O scorcher of foes —

sanskrit: ulūpī cintayām āsa tadā saṃjīvanaṃ maṇim sa copātiṣṭhata tadā pannagānāṃ parāyaṇam
english: Ulūpī then called to mind the life-restoring gem, and it came at once to her, that supreme refuge of the serpents.

sanskrit: taṃ gṛhītvā tu kauravya nāgarājapateḥ sutā manaḥprahlādanīṃ vācaṃ sainikānām athābravīt
english: Taking it up, O Kauravya, the daughter of the lord of the serpent-kings spoke to the soldiers words that gladdened the heart.

sanskrit: uttiṣṭha mā śucaḥ putra naiṣa jiṣṇus tvayā hataḥ ajeyaḥ puruṣair eṣa devair vāpi savāsavaiḥ
english: Rise up, do not grieve, my son! This Jiṣṇu was not slain by you; he cannot be conquered by men, nor even by the gods with Vāsava at their head.

sanskrit: mayā tu mohinī nāma māyaiṣā saṃprayojitā priyārthaṃ puruṣendrasya pitus te 'dya yaśasvinaḥ
english: It was I who deployed this illusion called Mohinī, this very day, for the sake of pleasing the lord of men, your glorious father.

sanskrit: jijñāsur hy eṣa vai putra balasya tava kauravaḥ saṃgrāme yudhyato rājann āgataḥ paravīrahā
english: For this Kaurava, wishing to test your strength, my son — that slayer of enemy heroes — came, O king, to do battle with you in combat.

sanskrit: tasmād asi mayā putra yuddhārthaṃ paricoditaḥ mā pāpam ātmanaḥ putra śaṅkethās tv aṇv api prabho
english: Therefore, my son, you were urged by me to give battle; do not suspect any sin in yourself, my son, not even the slightest, O lord.

sanskrit: ṛṣir eṣa mahātejāḥ puruṣaḥ śāśvato 'vyayaḥ nainaṃ śakto hi saṃgrāme jetuṃ śakro 'pi putraka
english: This man is a seer of great splendor, eternal and imperishable; not even Śakra is able to conquer him in battle, my little son.

sanskrit: ayaṃ tu me maṇir divyaḥ samānīto viśāṃ pate mṛtān mṛtān pannagendrān yo jīvayati nityadā
english: And this divine gem of mine I have brought, O lord of peoples — the one that ever and again brings back to life the serpent-lords who have died.

sanskrit: etam asyorasi tvaṃ tu sthāpayasva pituḥ prabho saṃjīvitaṃ punaḥ putra tato draṣṭāsi pāṇḍavam
english: Place this upon your father's breast, O lord; then, my son, you shall behold the son of Pāṇḍu restored to life once more.

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sthāpayām āsa tasyorasi maṇiṃ tadā pārthasyāmitatejāḥ sa pituḥ snehād apāpakṛt
english: Thus addressed, he then placed the gem upon the breast of Pārtha, that one of boundless splendor, out of love for his father, he who had done no sin.

sanskrit: tasmin nyaste maṇau vīra jiṣṇur ujjīvitaḥ prabhuḥ suptotthita ivottasthau mṛṣṭalohitalocanaḥ
english: When that gem was set in place, O hero, the lord Jiṣṇu was revived; he rose up as if waking from sleep, rubbing his reddened eyes.

sanskrit: tam utthitaṃ mahātmānaṃ labdhasaṃjñaṃ manasvinam samīkṣya pitaraṃ svasthaṃ vavande babhruvāhanaḥ
english: Beholding his father risen, the great-souled and wise one restored to consciousness and well, Babhruvāhana saluted him.

sanskrit: utthite puruṣavyāghre punar lakṣmīvati prabho divyāḥ sumanasaḥ puṇyā vavṛṣe pākaśāsanaḥ
english: When that tiger among men had risen again in all his splendor, O lord, the chastiser of Pāka rained down divine and holy blossoms.

sanskrit: anāhatā dundubhayaḥ praṇedur meghanisvanāḥ sādhu sādhv iti cākāśe babhūva sumahān svanaḥ
english: Drums, unstruck, resounded with the voice of thunderclouds, and there arose in the sky a mighty cry of 'Well done! Well done!'

sanskrit: utthāya tu mahābāhuḥ paryāśvasto dhanaṃjayaḥ babhruvāhanam āliṅgya samājighrata mūrdhani
english: Having risen, the mighty-armed Dhanaṃjaya, now revived, embraced Babhruvāhana and kissed him upon the head.

sanskrit: dadarśa cāvidūre 'sya mātaraṃ śokakarśitām ulūpyā saha tiṣṭhantīṃ tato 'pṛcchad dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: And he saw not far off his son's mother, wasted with grief, standing together with Ulūpī; then Dhanaṃjaya asked:

sanskrit: kim idaṃ lakṣyate sarvaṃ śokavismayaharṣavat raṇājiram amitraghna yadi jānāsi śaṃsa me
english: What is all this that appears here, this battlefield marked with grief and wonder and joy, O slayer of foes? If you know, tell me.

sanskrit: jananī ca kimarthaṃ te raṇabhūmim upāgatā nāgendraduhitā ceyam ulūpī kim ihāgatā
english: And why has your mother come to the field of battle, and why has this Ulūpī, daughter of the serpent-king, come hither?

sanskrit: jānāmy aham idaṃ yuddhaṃ tvayā madvacanāt kṛtam strīṇām āgamane hetum aham icchāmi veditum
english: I know that this battle was waged by you at my bidding; but the reason for these women's coming I wish to learn.

sanskrit: tam uvāca tataḥ pṛṣṭo maṇipūrapatis tadā prasādya śirasā vidvān ulūpī pṛcchyatām iti
english: Then the lord of Maṇipūra, thus questioned, the wise one, bowed his head in entreaty and said to him: 'Let Ulūpī be asked.'

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca kim āgamanakṛtyaṃ te kauravyakulanandini maṇipūrapater mātus tathaiva ca raṇājire
english: Arjuna said: What is the purpose of your coming, O delight of the Kaurava line, and likewise that of the mother of the lord of Maṇipūra, here upon the battlefield?

sanskrit: kaccit kuśalakāmāsi rājño 'sya bhujagātmaje mama vā cañcalāpāṅge kaccit tvaṃ śubham icchasi
english: Do you wish well to this king, O serpent's daughter, or to me, you of the restless glances? Do you desire good for us?

sanskrit: kaccit te pṛthulaśroṇi nāpriyaṃ śubhadarśane akārṣam aham ajñānād ayaṃ vā babhruvāhanaḥ
english: I hope, O broad-hipped one of fair appearance, that I have done nothing unwelcome to you in ignorance, nor has this Babhruvāhana.

sanskrit: kaccic ca rājaputrī te sapatnī caitravāhinī citrāṅgadā varārohā nāparādhyati kiṃ cana
english: And I hope that the princess, your co-wife of the line of Citravāhana, the fair-limbed Citrāṅgadā, has in no way given offense.

sanskrit: tam uvācoragapater duhitā prahasanty atha na me tvam aparāddho 'si na nṛpo babhruvāhanaḥ na janitrī tathāsyeyaṃ mama yā preṣyavat sthitā
english: Then the daughter of the serpent-lord answered him with a smile: Neither have you offended me, nor has King Babhruvāhana, nor this his mother, who stands by me like a servant.

sanskrit: śrūyatāṃ yad yathā cedaṃ mayā sarvaṃ viceṣṭitam na me kopas tvayā kāryaḥ śirasā tvāṃ prasādaye
english: Let it be heard how and why all this was contrived by me; you must not be angry with me — with bowed head I entreat you.

sanskrit: tvatprītyarthaṃ hi kauravya kṛtam etan mayānagha yat tac chṛṇu mahābāho nikhilena dhanaṃjaya
english: For it was for your sake, O Kauravya, that this was done by me, sinless one; hear it in full, O mighty-armed Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: mahābhāratayuddhe yat tvayā śāṃtanavo nṛpaḥ adharmeṇa hataḥ pārtha tasyaiṣā niṣkṛtiḥ kṛtā
english: In the great war of the Bhāratas, the king who was Śaṃtanu's son was slain by you unrighteously, O Pārtha; this is the atonement made for that.

sanskrit: na hi bhīṣmas tvayā vīra yudhyamāno nipātitaḥ śikhaṇḍinā tu saṃsaktas tam āśritya hatas tvayā
english: For Bhīṣma was not struck down by you, O hero, while he was fighting; engaged with Śikhaṇḍin, and using him as a shield, you slew him.

sanskrit: tasya śāntim akṛtvā tu tyajes tvaṃ yadi jīvitam karmaṇā tena pāpena patethā niraye dhruvam
english: Had you given up your life without performing the expiation for that deed, by that sinful act you would surely have fallen into hell.

sanskrit: eṣā tu vihitā śāntiḥ putrād yāṃ prāptavān asi vasubhir vasudhāpāla gaṅgayā ca mahāmate
english: But this expiation was ordained, which you have received at your son's hands, by the Vasus, O guardian of the earth, and by Gaṅgā, O greatly wise one.

sanskrit: purā hi śrutam etad vai vasubhiḥ kathitaṃ mayā gaṅgāyās tīram āgamya hate śāṃtanave nṛpe
english: For long ago I heard this, told by the Vasus, when, after King Śaṃtanu's son had been slain, they came to the bank of the Gaṅgā.

sanskrit: āplutya devā vasavaḥ sametya ca mahānadīm idam ūcur vaco ghoraṃ bhāgīrathyā mate tadā
english: Having bathed and gathered at the great river, the Vasu gods then spoke these terrible words, with the consent of Bhāgīrathī:

sanskrit: eṣa śāṃtanavo bhīṣmo nihataḥ savyasācinā ayudhyamānaḥ saṃgrāme saṃsakto 'nyena bhāmini
english: This Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, has been slain by Savyasācin while he was not fighting, being engaged with another in the combat, O fair lady.

sanskrit: tad anenābhiṣaṅgeṇa vayam apy arjunaṃ śubhe śāpena yojayāmeti tathāstv iti ca sābravīt
english: Therefore, on account of this assault, we too, O fair one, shall lay a curse upon Arjuna — so they said; and she replied, 'So be it.'

sanskrit: tad ahaṃ pitur āvedya bhṛśaṃ pravyathitendriyā abhavaṃ sa ca tac chrutvā viṣādam agamat param
english: Having reported this to my father, I became deeply distressed in all my senses; and he, hearing it, fell into the utmost despair.

sanskrit: pitā tu me vasūn gatvā tvadarthaṃ samayācata punaḥ punaḥ prasādyaināṃs ta enam idam abruvan
english: But my father went to the Vasus and pleaded for your sake, again and again entreating them; and they spoke this to him:

sanskrit: punas tasya mahābhāga maṇipūreśvaro yuvā sa enaṃ raṇamadhyasthaṃ śaraiḥ pātayitā bhuvi
english: The young lord of Maṇipūra, O greatly blessed one, his very son, shall fell him to the ground with arrows as he stands in the midst of battle;

sanskrit: evaṃ kṛte sa nāgendra muktaśāpo bhaviṣyati gaccheti vasubhiś cokto mama cedaṃ śaśaṃsa saḥ
english: when this is done, O serpent-king, he shall be released from the curse. 'Go,' he was told by the Vasus; and he related this to me.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā tvaṃ mayā tasmāc chāpād asi vimokṣitaḥ na hi tvāṃ devarājo 'pi samareṣu parājayet
english: Having heard this, I have freed you from that curse; for not even the king of the gods could defeat you in battle.

sanskrit: ātmā putraḥ smṛtas tasmāt tenehāsi parājitaḥ nātra doṣo mama mataḥ kathaṃ vā manyase vibho
english: The son is held to be one's own self; therefore you were defeated here by him. In this I see no fault — what do you think, O lord?

sanskrit: ity evam ukto vijayaḥ prasannātmābravīd idam sarvaṃ me supriyaṃ devi yad etat kṛtavaty asi
english: Thus addressed, Vijaya, his soul now serene, said this: All that you have done, O lady, is most pleasing to me.

sanskrit: ity uktvāthābravīt putraṃ maṇipūreśvaraṃ jayaḥ citrāṅgadāyāḥ śṛṇvantyāḥ kauravyaduhitus tathā
english: Having spoken thus, Jaya then addressed his son, the lord of Maṇipūra, while Citrāṅgadā and the daughter of the Kaurava listened:

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhirasyāśvamedhaḥ parāṃ caitrīṃ bhaviṣyati tatrāgaccheḥ sahāmātyo mātṛbhyāṃ sahito nṛpa
english: Yudhiṣṭhira's horse-sacrifice will take place on the coming full moon of Caitra; come there, O king, with your ministers and together with your mothers.

sanskrit: ity evam uktaḥ pārthena sa rājā babhruvāhanaḥ uvāca pitaraṃ dhīmān idam asrāvilekṣaṇaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Pārtha, that king Babhruvāhana, the wise one, with eyes clouded by tears, said this to his father:

sanskrit: upayāsyāmi dharmajña bhavataḥ śāsanād aham aśvamedhe mahāyajñe dvijātipariveṣakaḥ
english: I shall come, O knower of duty, at your command, to the great sacrifice of the horse, to serve the twice-born there.

sanskrit: mama tv anugrahārthāya praviśasva puraṃ svakam bhāryābhyāṃ saha śatrughna mā bhūt te 'tra vicāraṇā
english: But to do me a favor, enter your own city together with your two wives, O slayer of foes; let there be no hesitation in you about this.

sanskrit: uṣitveha viśalyas tvaṃ sukhaṃ sve veśmani prabho punar aśvānugamanaṃ kartāsi jayatāṃ vara
english: Having dwelt here at ease in your own dwelling, your wounds healed, O lord, you may again take up the following of the horse, O best of the victorious.

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa tu putreṇa tadā vānaraketanaḥ smayan provāca kaunteyas tadā citrāṅgadāsutam
english: Thus addressed by his son, that one whose banner bore the ape, the son of Kuntī, then smiling spoke to the son of Citrāṅgadā:

sanskrit: viditaṃ te mahābāho yathā dīkṣāṃ carāmy aham na sa tāvat pravekṣyāmi puraṃ te pṛthulocana
english: You know, O mighty-armed one, how I am bound by my consecration; therefore I shall not enter your city, O wide-eyed one.

sanskrit: yathākāmaṃ prayāty eṣa yajñiyaś ca turaṃgamaḥ svasti te 'stu gamiṣyāmi na sthānaṃ vidyate mama
english: This sacrificial steed goes where it will; may it be well with you — I must depart, for no stopping is allowed me.

sanskrit: sa tatra vidhivat tena pūjitaḥ pākaśāsaniḥ bhāryābhyām abhyanujñātaḥ prāyād bharatasattamaḥ
english: There, duly honored by him, the son of the chastiser of Pāka, taking leave of his two wives, departed — that best of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sa tu vājī samudrāntāṃ paryetya pṛthivīm imām nivṛtto 'bhimukho rājan yena nāgāhvayaṃ puram
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: But that horse, having wandered round this earth bounded by the ocean, turned back, O king, heading toward the city named for the elephant.

sanskrit: anugacchaṃś ca tejasvī nivṛtto 'tha kirīṭabhṛt yadṛcchayā samāpede puraṃ rājagṛhaṃ tadā
english: And the splendid wearer of the diadem, following it back, by chance came then upon the city of Rājagṛha.

sanskrit: tam abhyāśagataṃ rājā jarāsaṃdhātmajātmajaḥ kṣatradharme sthito vīraḥ samarāyājuhāva ha
english: As he drew near, the king who was the grandson of Jarāsaṃdha, a hero steadfast in the law of the warrior, summoned him to battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ purāt sa niṣkramya rathī dhanvī śarī talī meghasaṃdhiḥ padātiṃ taṃ dhanaṃjayam upādravat
english: Then, issuing from the city, mounted on his chariot, bow and arrows and hand-guard ready, Meghasaṃdhi rushed upon Dhanaṃjaya, who was on foot.

sanskrit: āsādya ca mahātejā meghasaṃdhir dhanaṃjayam bālabhāvān mahārāja provācedaṃ na kauśalāt
english: And drawing near to Dhanaṃjaya, the greatly splendid Meghasaṃdhi, out of boyishness, O great king, and not from skill, spoke thus:

sanskrit: kim ayaṃ cāryate vājī strīmadhya iva bhārata hayam enaṃ hariṣyāmi prayatasva vimokṣaṇe
english: Why is this horse being led about as though in the midst of women, O Bhārata? I shall carry this steed off; make your effort to set it free.

sanskrit: adattānunayo yuddhe yadi tvaṃ pitṛbhir mama kariṣyāmi tavātithyaṃ prahara praharāmi vā
english: If you were not taught submission in battle by my forefathers, I shall show you hospitality; strike, or I shall strike.

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ pratyuvācainaṃ pāṇḍavaḥ prahasann iva vighnakartā mayā vārya iti me vratam āhitam
english: Thus addressed, the son of Pāṇḍu answered him with something like a laugh: It is my vow laid down that whoever raises obstruction must be warded off by me.

sanskrit: bhrātrā jyeṣṭhena nṛpate tavāpi viditaṃ dhruvam praharasva yathāśakti na manyur vidyate mama
english: This was enjoined by my eldest brother, O king, and is surely known to you as well; strike to the best of your power — there is no anger in me.

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ prāharat pūrvaṃ pāṇḍavaṃ magadheśvaraḥ kirañ śarasahasrāṇi varṣāṇīva sahasradṛk
english: Thus addressed, the lord of Magadha struck first at the son of Pāṇḍu, scattering thousands of arrows as the thousand-eyed one pours down rains.

sanskrit: tato gāṇḍīvabhṛc chūro gāṇḍīvapreṣitaiḥ śaraiḥ cakāra moghāṃs tān bāṇān ayatnād bharatarṣabha
english: Then the heroic bearer of the Gāṇḍīva, with arrows sped from the Gāṇḍīva, rendered those shafts vain without effort, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: sa moghaṃ tasya bāṇaughaṃ kṛtvā vānaraketanaḥ śarān mumoca jvalitān dīptāsyān iva pannagān
english: Having made the flood of his arrows fruitless, he of the ape-banner loosed blazing shafts like serpents with flaming mouths.

sanskrit: dhvaje patākādaṇḍeṣu rathayantre hayeṣu ca anyeṣu ca rathāṅgeṣu na śarīre na sārathau
english: Upon the banner, upon the staffs of the pennants, upon the chariot's frame and the horses, and upon the other parts of the car — but not upon the body, nor upon the charioteer.

sanskrit: saṃrakṣyamāṇaḥ pārthena śarīre phalgunasya ha manyamānaḥ svavīryaṃ tan māgadhaḥ prāhiṇoc charān
english: Being thus spared by Pārtha as to his body, the man of Magadha, taking this for his own valor, kept loosing his arrows at Phalguna.

sanskrit: tato gāṇḍīvabhṛc chūro māgadhena samāhataḥ babhau vāsantika iva palāśaḥ puṣpito mahān
english: Then the heroic bearer of the Gāṇḍīva, struck by the Magadhan, shone like a great palāśa tree of spring covered with blossoms.

sanskrit: avadhyamānaḥ so 'bhyaghnan māgadhaḥ pāṇḍavarṣabham tena tasthau sa kauravya lokavīrasya darśane
english: Not being slain himself, the Magadhan went on striking the bull of the Pāṇḍavas; and by that, O Kauravya, he held his ground in the sight of the world's hero.

sanskrit: savyasācī tu saṃkruddho vikṛṣya balavad dhanuḥ hayāṃś cakāra nirdehān sāratheś ca śiro 'harat
english: But Savyasācin, wrathful, drawing his bow with might, made the horses lifeless and struck off the charioteer's head.

sanskrit: dhanuś cāsya mahac citraṃ kṣureṇa pracakarta ha hastāvāpaṃ patākāṃ ca dhvajaṃ cāsya nyapātayat
english: And with a razor-edged arrow he cut apart that great and splendid bow of his, and brought down his hand-guard, his pennant, and his banner.
